{{short description|American mathematician (1936–2008)}}
{{More footnotes|date=September 2021}}
'''Robert Evert Stong''' (August 23, 1936, [[Oklahoma City]] – April 10, 2008, [[Charlottesville, Virginia]]) was a mathematician at the [[University of Virginia]] who proved the [[Hattori–Stong theorem]].

==Early life and education==
Stong received a B.A. and M.A. in mathematics at the [[University of Oklahoma]].{{cn|date=September 2021}} He received a Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1962.<ref name="genealogy"/> His Ph.D. dissertation, ''Some relations among characteristic classes and numbers'', was written under the supervision of [[Richard Lashof]].<ref name="genealogy"/> He served on active duty with the [[United States Army Reserve]]s from 1962 to 1965 and was stationed at [[Fort Benjamin Harrison]] and [[the Pentagon]]. He worked on computer development and rose to the rank of captain.

==Career==
After serving with the Army, he went to the [[University of Oxford]] as a post-doctoral fellow (1964–66), and then to [[Princeton University]] as faculty (1966–68). In 1968 he became Professor of Mathematics at the University of Virginia, where he taught until his retirement in 2007. With Landweber and Ravenel, Stong introduced [[elliptic cohomology]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=redden |first1=corbett |title=ELLIPTIC COHOMOLOGY: A HISTORICAL OVERVIEW |url=https://users.math.msu.edu/users/redden/EllipticCohomology.pdf}}</ref>

His doctoral students included [[Nelson Saiers]].<ref name="genealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=6510}}</ref>
